body.title: The Celestial Wedding and the River Crossing: Chithirai Thiruvizha and Regional Harmony
body.orientation: How a month-long temple festival brought Shaivite and Vaishnavite traditions together in the sacred riverbed of the Vaigai.

hero.alt: Grand wooden temple chariot of Meenakshi Temple pulled by thousands of devotees in Madurai

paragraphs.text: The Chithirai Festival of Madurai, celebrated in the Tamil month of Chithirai (April–May), is one of the world's longest continuously observed temple festivals, spanning nearly a month.

King Thirumalai Nayak in the 17th century politically united two previously separate festivals: the celestial wedding of Meenakshi and Sundareswarar, and Lord Alagar's journey from Alagar Koyil into the Vaigai River.

sections.heading: The golden horse in the riverbed

paragraphs.text: The dramatic climax occurs when Lord Alagar enters the Vaigai River mounted on a golden horse, greeted by over a million pilgrims in the dry summer riverbed.
Chithirai Thiruvizha demonstrates how enlightened statesmanship utilized sacred ritual and riverfront topography to forge enduring peace between rival religious communities.

followUpQuestions: Why does Lord Alagar turn back without attending the wedding ceremony?
How do agricultural communities around Madurai participate in pulling the giant temple car (Ther)?

claims.text: Chithirai Festival spans nearly an entire month of rituals across Madurai and the Vaigai River.

evidence.excerpt: The Chithirai festival is one of the biggest celebrations in Madurai, lasting for nearly a month during the Tamil month of Chithirai.

claims.text: King Thirumalai Nayak combined the Shaivite Meenakshi wedding with the Vaishnavite Alagar festival.

evidence.excerpt: Ruler Thirumalai Nayak merged the two separate festivals into a single grand celebration to unite Shaivites and Vaishnavites.

claims.text: Lord Alagar enters the Vaigai River mounted on a golden horse, observed by massive crowds.

evidence.excerpt: The highlight of the festival is Lord Alagar's grand entry into the Vaigai River riding his golden horse.

claims.text: The festival served as a social mechanism for communal harmony across regional caste and sectarian lines.

evidence.excerpt: Scholars emphasize the role of the festival in promoting sectarian solidarity across diverse communities of the region.
